name: ServiceNow Telecom Service Operations Management (TSOM)
why: TSOM is purpose-built for communications service providers (CSPs). It manages the lifecycle of telecom services—from order capture through activation, assurance, and billing—using telecom-specific data models, inventory, and orchestration.
breadcrumbs: All > Telecom Service Operations > Service Inventory > ...
All > Telecom Service Operations > Network Inventory > ...
All > Telecom Service Operations > Service Orders > All
All > Telecom Service Operations > Alarms > All

guided_setup.path: All > Telecom Service Operations > Administration > Guided Setup

critical.why: Auto-number; unique service identifier
Draft → Pending → Active → Suspended → Retired
Voice, Data, VPN, TV, Mobile
Who owns the service
Management IP address
Circuit capacity (e.g., 1Gbps)
Critical, Major, Minor, Warning

must_know: TSOM is a scoped application (com.snc.tsom); cross-scope access required for global table access.
Service Orders drive provisioning; Services are the logical result.
Alarms correlate to network elements, which relate to services.
Inventory items (ONTs, modems, SIMs) are tracked separately from services.
quiz: What is the primary table for telecom services?
What table stores physical network elements?
What is the difference between a service and a service order?

name: ServiceNow Customer Service Management (CSM)
why: ITSM pointed outward: cases, accounts, entitlements, SLAs against paying customers, and a portal that customers actually use. CSM includes a customer-facing portal, agent workspace, and entitlement-based SLAs.
breadcrumbs: All > Customer Service > Administration > Case Types
All > Customer Service > Customer Service Portal

critical.why: Everything (entitlement, SLA, reporting) hangs off the account.
Who reported it; drives auth and comms.
Decides whether service is included.
Selects workflow and required fields.
Contractual, not internal, promise.

must_know: Entitlement checks are the CSM-specific twist; without them SLAs are guesses.
External users are real users with ACLs — test as the customer, not as admin.
Case types are the CSM equivalent of catalog items: they define what an agent can even do.
mistakes: One case type for every request
quiz: What decides if service is included?
Where do customer-visible SLAs come from?

name: ServiceNow Field Service Management (FSM)
why: Scheduling + mobile work: work orders, tasks, territories, and the constraint engine. The visual (dispatch map) hides a lot of configuration.
breadcrumbs: All > Field Service Management > Work Orders > All
All > Field Service Management > Dispatch > Dispatch Board
All > Field Service Management > Administration > Territories
All > Field Service Management > Administration > Scheduling > Constraints

guided_setup.path: All > Field Service Management > Guided Setup

critical.why: Primary routing constraint; wrong territory = unassignable work.
Drives the whole scheduling engine and customer promise.
Who actually does the work.
Skill matching decides eligibility.
Travel time and dispatch map depend on coordinates.

must_know: Work order = the business ask; task = the visit; assignment = who/when. Three tables, three concepts.
Constraints (skills, territory, hours) are configuration, not code — but bad data makes the engine look broken.
Mobile behavior must be tested on Now Mobile, not desktop.
quiz: Difference between work order, task, assignment?
What are the three main scheduling constraints?

name: ServiceNow Sales CRM
why: ServiceNow Sales CRM is the platform's customer relationship management application, built on the same ServiceNow platform as ITSM and CSM but optimized for sales pipeline management. Sales CRM tracks leads, opportunities, accounts, contacts, quotes, and orders—giving sales teams a single system of record from prospect to closed deal.

critical.why: Customer account name; drives entitlement and SLA.
Prospecting → Qualification → Proposal → Negotiation → Closed Won/Lost.
Expected deal value; drives pipeline forecasting.
When the deal is expected to close; drives forecasting.
Quote expiration date.
Total quote amount.

must_know: Sales CRM is built on the same platform as ITSM and CSM but optimized for sales pipeline management.
Lead → Opportunity → Quote → Order is the standard sales flow.
Entitlement checks are the CSM-specific twist; Sales CRM uses opportunity stages instead.
External users are real users with ACLs — test as the sales rep, not as admin.
mistakes: Not updating stage as deal progresses
quiz: What field determines which sales workflow fires?
What is the difference between an account and a contact?

name: ServiceNow Hardware Asset Management (HAM)
why: Hardware Asset Management (HAM) is the hardware-focused subset of ServiceNow IT Asset Management (ITAM). HAM tracks physical IT assets—laptops, servers, monitors, phones, printers, and other hardware—from procurement through disposal.
breadcrumbs: All > Asset Management > Administration > Asset Models

flows: Asset lifecycle flows (procure → receive → deploy → maintain → retire)
integrations: Service Graph Connectors (Intune/SCCM/Jamf → hardware + software installs)

critical.why: Human key; must be unique and sticker-aligned.
Determines which fields appear.
Lifecycle truth: on order / in stock / in use / retired.
Manufacturer serial; warranty link.
Warranty start, depreciation.
Custody. Missing owner = lost asset.

must_know: Assets (alm_asset) and CIs (cmdb_ci) are different records that point at each other. One asset can map to one CI; not everything is an asset.
SAM Pro needs the software install data feed (SCCM/Intune/agent) or the license position is fiction.
Licence compliance = rights (entitlement) vs installs/usage; you need both sides.
mistakes: Buying assets without creating asset records first
quiz: What is the difference between alm_asset and cmdb_ci?
Which table holds software license information?
What are the asset lifecycle states?

name: ServiceNow IT Service Management (ITSM)
why: ITSM is ServiceNow's flagship application for managing IT services. ITSM covers Incident, Problem, Change, Change Task, Knowledge, and Configuration Management. It is the reference implementation of the platform—every other module follows the same patterns.

critical.why: Auto-number; the only identifier users quote. Never edit by hand.
Who is affected. Wrong caller = wrong SLA, wrong comms, wrong reports.
Mandatory by dictionary on OOB; the searchable summary.
Routing. If this is empty, nothing else you configure will get the ticket worked.
Drives SLA pause/resume, close rules, and reporting. Changing state order breaks automation.
These compute priority. Priority is usually derived, not typed.
Enforced at close by OOB UI policy; blank closes corrupt reporting.

must_know: incident extends task. Everything you learn about 'task' fields applies to incident, problem, change, and catalog tasks.
Priority = f(impact, urgency) through a matrix (Data Lookup), not something agents type.
An SLA is a task_sla record attached to the incident; the SLA definition decides start/pause/stop conditions.
Closing requires close_code + close_notes in OOB; that is a UI policy, so it is invisible in the dictionary.
mistakes: Adding a custom field when an unused OOB field already exists
Editing state choices without checking SLA and flow conditions
Testing as admin only — admin bypasses ACLs
Deleting demo users, which breaks OOB flow references
quiz: Which fields determine priority, and where is that matrix defined?
What record type implements an SLA on a given incident?
Name three things that break if you reorder state values.
